This claim petition is filed u/s 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 05.04.2022 at about 11.30 a.m, as the petitioner was crossing the road carefully and by observing the vehicle movements near Melumalai Bus Stop, situated on Krishnagiri - Hosur NH road, Tamil Nadu at that time suddenly the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MH-0917 came with high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to tremendous impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to near by hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment.

It is is alleged that for further management he was referred to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent several surgeries.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
Due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident.
She fully disabled to avocation and loss earning capacity.
Looking to the nature of injuries he permanently disabled.
The accident was caused due to rash and negligence driving of the car, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the vehicle are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement denied the issuance of policy in respect of car.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of car is denied by this respondent and contended that the accident took place due to the negligence of petitioner himself.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a road traffic accident on 05.04.2022 at about 11.30 a.m, near Melumalai Bus Stop, on Krishnagiri - Hosur NH road, Tamil Nadu and sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MH-0917 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

Ex's.P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.

K.J.C was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.14 to 16 documents.
Dr. Shailesh A.V.Rao, Neurosurgeon was examined as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.17 to 22 documents.
Further the petitioner also examined his employer as PW.4, through him got marked Ex.P.23 to 29 documents.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.40,00,000/- together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the car Reg.No.KA-53-MH-0917 for the offences punishable under section's 279, 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the car.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
10. ISSUE NO.2:

As per the medical records, PW.1 has sustained the following injuries : 1) Abrasion over temporal aspect of left side of head 2) Laceration over anterior aspect of lover 1/3rd of the leg,
abnormal mobility 3) Abrasion over left side of neck.
It is needless to say that injury No.1 & are simple and injury No.2 grievous in nature.

The Discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.8 to 10 indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital from 06.04.2022 to 04.05.2022 (28 days) and at Srinivasa Hospital from 17.06.2022 to 19.06.2022 (3 days) and at Premier Health Care from 04.05.2022 to 13.05.2022 (10 days).
In total he took treatment for a period of 41 days.

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : ORIF with IMIL done for fracture of both bone right leg distal 1/3rd under SAB.
11.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Chidanand. K.J.C as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 43% and 14% disability to the whole body.

It is Avinash H.N vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27436248/

sentences.text: He admitted that all the fractures are united and from the date of discharge till his assessment, there was a considerable improvement in the condition of the patient.
He admitted that the petitioner can do day-to-day activities with certain difficulties.

12. Further more the petitioner has also got examined Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao, Consultant Neurosurgeon as PW.3 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found the petitioner sustained frontal contusion, fracture of both bones of right leg.
He was mechanical ventilator.
Further he stated that the patient with scars on right leg.
He was ambulant with support of one person.
He had spastic weakness on left side.
He had cognitive and memory deficits.
He had impaired smell and hearing loss on left side.
He had diplopia on looking towards left.
He stated that MMSE was doe on 25.07.2023, which revealed a score of 21/30 which is low.
Further Audio- metry test was done on 24.02.2024 this was suggestive of profound sensori neural hearing loss in left ear.
Further the neuro psychological assessment was done on 02.03.2024, wherein his IQ was 54 (normal range being 90-109).
He was below average in thinking and reasoning.
He was in the range of Mild Mental Retradation.
His frontal, temporal, occipital and parietal lobes were slow and inadequate in functioning.
His IDEAS score was 7, suggestive of 40 to 70% disability.

The MRI brain was done on 02.03.2024, it revealed cerebral atrophy, multiple bilateral chronic micro hemorrhages, left thalamic scaring and after through investigation the petitioner sustained following disabilities.

1) Cognitive disability (IQ 54), 2) left ear profound sensori neural hearing loss,
3) Spastic weakness of left side 4) Impairment of smell, 5) Double vision.
Further he found that the petitioner has sustained 55% disability to the whole body and is likely to be permanent.
If the cross- examination of PW.4 is perused, it becomes clear that he has not treated the petitioner.
He admitted that he was a neurosurgeon but not neuro psychologist.
He stated that for head injury he was taken conservative treatment, for right leg bone fracture, he was operated and mechanical ventilator.
Duration of mechanical ventilator was not mentioned in discharge summary.
At the time of discharge from Sanjay Gandhi hospital he was advised for physiotherapy and medication.
He was also referred to NIMHANS for management of head injury.
He further admitted that that at Sanjay Gandhi hospital petitioner was not underwent surgical treatment for head injury.
They have not submitted documents of NIMHANS hospital, subsequently petitioner approached Premier Health Care, Bengaluru.
Petitioner has taken conservative treatment for head injury at Premier Health care hospital.
He admitted that no brain surgery to petitioner.
Further PW.3 stated that he has not tested audiogram test to the petitioner.
Further as per MRI there was mild brain atrophy.
Further he admitted that in Ex.P.22 MRI, injuries were not seen and as per the original CT Scan taken soon after the head injury only right frontal contusion.
He further admitted that the petitioner has taken conservative treatment for head injury and advised for physiotherapy.
13. Anyhow from a careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 & 3 have assessed the disability on the higher side.

Even otherwise considering the fact that the petitioner could appear before the Tribunal, lead his evidence and not only understand the questions put to him in the course of cross-examination but also give proper answers to them, the percentage of disability assessed by PW.2 & 3 is highly exaggerated.

sentences.text: LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
Now it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.

The petitioner deposed that he was working as Accountant in Petrol Bunk and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and that after accident he was unable to do any work and suffering from permanent disability and loss his future.
In order to prove the said fact the petitioner has examined his employer as PW.4.

PW.4 has produced Ex.P.24 to 29 being Appointment letter,
Pay slips for the months of January-2022 to March 2022, Employer ID card, statement of account of petitioner.
In his chief examination he stated that he didn't know if their company was registered under company law or not.
Total of 1200 people work in their company.
They supply workers to private companies and government companies.
They pay the salaries of the workers themselves.
The original employer pays the salary to their company.
They pay the workers.
They deposit the salary into employees account.
He stated that now the salary mentioned in the Ex.P.25 that he was looking at is the total salary and does not include bonus.
Including basic, DA and bonus, the total salary shown in the Ex.P.25 is Rs.22,392, so that is correct.
He stated that they have increased the salary time to time as per the rules of Minimum Wages Act.
He stated that petitioner was their permanent employee.
He clearly stated that petitioner has not resigned the job and they have not removed him from the work.
When he saw him he was not able to work.
Therefore they have not been paid the salary to him.
15. It is pertinent to note in the cross examination PW.1 categorically admitted that he has not produced the documents to show that he was not working in the said petrol bunk.
Non- production of these documents leads to drawing of an adverse inference that the petitioner has continued carrying on his avocation.
Meaning thereby he has not sustained any financial loss on account of the accidental injuries suffered by him.
Furthermore the documents clearly depicts that the income of the petitioner year wise increased.
There was no loss of income during the period of hospitalization.
Accordingly no credence can be attached to the contents of ExP.24 to 29.
Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
However it should be remembered that the petitioner has suffered physical impairment to the extent of 28% to his whole body.

Placing reliance upon the decision reported in ILR 2015 KAR 167 (Dr.Yeshwant Dongre V/s Salman Rasheed &
others), it deem just & proper to award a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- towards the disability suffered by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 16. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES:
The disability referred supra would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
17. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 41 days is proved.

As such during his stay in the Hospital, the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges, as some family member/s of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care, by leaving his/her duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards Avinash H.N vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27436248/
5 special diet, transportation and nutrition.

sentences.text: Accordingly considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day.
Hence Rs.49,200/- (1,200 X 41) is awarded under this head.
18. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner,
line and duration of treatment, he is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings undergone by him.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.2,53,233/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,53,233/- which is rounded off to Rs.2,53,200/- towards medical expenses.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The PW.2 doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.25,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.20,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.
21. The calculation table for PW.1, stands as follows; 1 Loss of income during laid-up : - NIL - period
2 Loss of future income : - NIL - 3 Towards Disability : 1,50,000-00 4 Loss of future amenities : 80,000-00 5 Attendant charges,
extra : 49,200-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 6 Pain and sufferings : 1,00,000-00
7 Medical Expenses : 2,53,200-00 8
Future medical expenses : 20,000-00 Total 6,52,400-00 22.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. It is contended in para 3 of the written statement that respondent No.1 has not issued any policy.
However policy which is found in documents, as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MH-0917 covering the date of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,52,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.

Draw award accordingly.
rpc_texts: Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,52,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
